metadata.title: Exploration of the Stacking Ensemble Machine Learning Algorithm for Cheating Detection in Large-Scale Assessment

design_fields.q1_rationale: The study does not use ILSA achievement data as an outcome or predictor, focusing instead on a cheating detection classification.
design_fields.q2_rationale: Matching text-readable full PDF has no explicit statement that ILSA sampling weights were omitted; weight references concern model parameters, outcome scaling, data variables or class/pixel weighting, not demonstrated sample-weight use.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study does not analyze student-level survey data where schools are the sampling unit, as it uses a licensure-test dataset.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The study mentions using k-fold cross-validation for model evaluation, indicating only internal validation.
design_fields._pdf_matched: 98. Zhou & Jiao. (2022). Exploration of the Stacking Ensemble Machine Learning Algorithm for Cheating Detection in Large-Scale Assessment.pdf
design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): The dataset consists of two test forms... made publicly available by Cizek and Wollack (2017). No information was given about the types of cheating behaviors... No information about countries/education systems or separate per-country analyses is provided.
design_fields._q2_audit: Source checked; original extraction rationale: The study explicitly states that it did not apply sampling weights and treats the dataset as a convenience sample.
